title: Grateful Dead Live at Golden Hall Community Concourse on 1970-08-05
lineage: SBD > MR > Reel > PCM > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Rare 1970 all‑acoustic set featuring a stellar El Paso and Ballad of Casey Jones, captured on a hiss‑y soundboard that’s fair but still rewarding.
ai_review.review: The show is praised as one of the finest early‑70s acoustic performances – listeners highlight the beautiful rendition of El Paso, Rosalie McFall, Cocaine Blues, Deep Elem Blues and the moving Ballad of Casey Jones.  The recording comes from a soundboard source that suffers from noticeable hiss, a muddy mix and an over‑prominent mandolin, which keeps the technical quality at a fair level but doesn’t diminish the historic value.  Overall fans consider it a treasured gem despite the vocal and mix shortcomings.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers (30+) give 4–5 stars, praising the performance while noting consistent recording flaws; the strong musical merit outweighs technical issues.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Noticeable tape hiss and a muddy mix; mandolin sits too high in the spectrum, vocals are low on several tracks, but overall sound is listenable for an acoustic set.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Laid‑back, almost church‑like pacing that lets the acoustic instrumentation breathe; the set feels like a relaxed campfire performance rather than a high‑energy rock show.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Mandolin work is highlighted (debated whether Jerry or David Nelson), guitar tone praised especially on "Lay Me Down".
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass described as restrained yet providing just enough weight for the acoustic texture.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mixed opinions – some note Kreutzmann's drumming as too busy, others think Mickey is behind the kit with a lighter, more diagonal feel.
